professional_standards_2027.heading: Learn Workplace Behaviours That Can Be Practised, Observed and Improved.
professional_standards_2027.copy: Develop practical teamwork and professional effectiveness skills through realistic exercises, constructive feedback and collaborative problem-solving. Learn to demonstrate responsibility, listening, adaptability and respectful communication without relying on personality labels or stereotypes.

corrections.principle: Professionalism Is Not a Personality Type
corrections.detail: Introverts are not inherently poor communicators, and extroverts are not inherently better leaders. Performance is evaluated strictly on relevant workplace task completion.

corrections.principle: Respect Does Not Mean Unquestioning Agreement
corrections.detail: Professional communication includes respectful clarification, evidence-based concerns, constructive disagreement, and ethical boundaries.

corrections.principle: Confidence Is Not a Universal Performance Measure
corrections.detail: Deliberate, careful communication demonstrates thoroughness and reliability. Evaluation measures communication effectiveness rather than theatrical bravado.

corrections.principle: Adaptability Does Not Mean Unlimited Workload
corrections.detail: True adaptability involves transparent capacity communication, realistic workload sequencing, and appropriate escalation—not unsustainable overwork.
Quiet task execution, accurate documentation, active listening, and supporting colleagues are as vital to teamwork as verbal participation.

corrections.principle: Emotional Intelligence Does Not Require Diagnosing Others
corrections.detail: Focuses on personal self-awareness, empathy, and professional responses rather than amateur psychological profiling or mental state diagnosis.

observable_behaviour_framework.heading: Assess What Students Do — Not What Personality They Appear to Have.

competencies.name: Listening
competencies.evidence: Allows speaker to explain fully, asks relevant clarifying questions, accurately paraphrases information, and responds directly to the message.

competencies.name: Cooperation
competencies.evidence: Fulfills agreed commitments, shares critical updates proactively, adheres to team charter agreements, and supports group deliverables.

competencies.name: Accountability
competencies.evidence: Confirms task ownership, tracks progress transparently, reports blockers early, acknowledges errors promptly, and implements corrective actions.

competencies.name: Feedback
competencies.evidence: Cites specific observable work behaviours, utilizes Situation-Behaviour-Impact (SBI), maintains professional tone, and suggests practical improvements.

competencies.name: Adaptability
competencies.evidence: Identifies changed project requirements, assesses ripple effects on schedule, negotiates priorities realistically, and updates stakeholders.

competencies.name: Problem-Solving
competencies.evidence: Clearly defines the core issue, distinguishes facts from assumptions, evaluates viable trade-offs, and recommends defensible solutions.

competencies.name: Conflict Management
competencies.evidence: Addresses routine disagreements calmly, separates the problem from the person, listens to diverse perspectives, and identifies agreed next steps.

conflict_safety_boundaries.heading: Learn When to Discuss, When to Clarify and When to Escalate.
conflict_safety_boundaries.routine_disagreements: Covers task ownership confusion, conflicting deadlines, missed handoffs, and differing technical approaches through active listening and constructive negotiation.
conflict_safety_boundaries.serious_workplace_issues: Explicitly distinguishes routine friction from serious misconduct such as harassment, discrimination, threats, or unsafe conditions. Students are taught institutional reporting pathways, HR policies, and escalation routes rather than attempting informal personal negotiation.
conflict_safety_boundaries.training_limits: This course teaches general workplace communication and effectiveness. It does not provide legal employment advice, HR dispute investigation credentials, or formal mediation licensure.

remote_and_hybrid_readiness.heading: Work Effectively Across In-Person and Remote Teams.
topics: Asynchronous Communication: Writing concise, unambiguous status updates, task briefs, and decision summaries.
Meeting Etiquette & Presence: Joining prepared, managing microphones, active chat participation, and camera-optional inclusive norms.
Distributed Accountability: Keeping progress visible on shared trackers, flagging dependencies early, and respecting time-zone differences.
Sustainable Boundaries: Establishing realistic working hours, clear response expectations, and avoiding burnout from constant availability.

responsible_ai_policy.heading: Use AI to Practise Workplace Decisions — Keep Human Judgment in Control.
responsible_ai_policy.approved_copy: Use AI assistants where appropriate to generate fictional workplace scenarios, review communication drafts and support reflection. Verify outputs, protect confidential information and make independent professional judgments.
appropriate_uses: Generating diverse fictional team scenarios and practice case studies
Simulating feedback role-plays and reviewing draft responses for constructive tone
Drafting options matrices and trade-off checklists for workplace problem-solving
Generating reflective questions to evaluate personal task management habits
mandatory_human_verification: Verify all facts, scenario realism, and organizational constraints manually
Ensure fairness, eliminate cultural bias, and verify ethical implications
Never upload confidential, proprietary, or personal workplace data to AI platforms
Maintain human judgment in all final decisions, evaluations, and interpersonal communications
prohibited_practices: Diagnosing student or colleague personality traits using AI text analysis
Ranking team members by AI-generated emotional intelligence or competence scores
Automating disciplinary feedback or replacing human facilitator evaluations with AI metrics
Inferring psychological or mental health conditions from workplace writing

safe_prompts.prompt: Create a fictional workplace scenario in which a colleague needs specific constructive feedback about a task. Include realistic facts, responsibilities and possible misunderstandings. Do not use personality labels, protected characteristics or psychological diagnoses. Provide an opportunity to practise respectful feedback.
Review this fictional team problem and identify three feasible options. Explain the assumptions, trade-offs and risks. Do not invent facts or claim that one approach is guaranteed to succeed.

Help me reflect on the observable behaviours described in this simulated teamwork activity. Identify examples of listening, task ownership, collaboration and decision-making. Do not infer personality traits or mental health. Suggest two specific behaviours I could practise.

inclusive_assessment.principles: Evaluation is grounded entirely in observable task execution, cooperation, and respectful interaction. Accommodates diverse communication preferences, cultural backgrounds, and neurodivergent thinking patterns.
inclusive_assessment.accommodations: Supports clear written instructions, explicit team roles, structured turn-taking, accessible document formats, and small-group collaboration options without penalizing different conversational pacing or nonverbal styles.

portfolio.title: Professional Effectiveness Portfolio — Teamwork, Adaptability & Workplace Behaviour
portfolio.description: A comprehensive, evidence-based workplace skills portfolio documenting practical team collaboration, task prioritization, constructive conflict handling, collaborative problem-solving, and a structured 30-day personal development plan.

deliverables.name: Component 01: Professional Team Charter
deliverables.description: Demonstrates the ability to establish clear shared working expectations, communication channels, role allocations, decision processes, and conflict resolution mechanisms in a team environment.
required_elements: Team name, project purpose, and shared objective
Clear team member roles and individual responsibilities
Communication channels and response time expectations
Meeting agreements, task tracking methods, and status cadences
Decision-making process and accountability standards
Inclusive collaboration guidelines and psychological safety
Conflict-handling process, escalation route, and review sign-off
evidence: Completed Team Charter document
Roles and responsibilities matrix
Working agreements record
Facilitator observation and team feedback

deliverables.name: Component 02: Workplace Prioritization & Time Management Plan
deliverables.description: Demonstrates practical time management, task sequencing, workload estimation, and professional adaptation to sudden priority shifts under realistic constraints.
required_elements: Task inventory (minimum 5 tasks with objectives, dependencies, and deadlines)
Urgency vs. Importance matrix classification
Workload capacity assumptions and realistic effort estimates
Resolution of one conflicting deadline and one unexpected requirement change
Professional stakeholder communication and boundary management
evidence: Prioritization spreadsheet / planner
Weekly task schedule and workload allocation
Written reasoning for trade-off decisions and boundary communication
Reflection on sustainable productivity habits

deliverables.name: Component 03: Two Assessed Workplace Role-Play Evaluations
deliverables.description: Two separately evaluated realistic workplace simulations assessing observable interpersonal behaviours: one routine conflict resolution scenario and one constructive feedback exchange.
required_elements: Role-Play A (Workplace Conflict): Clarify facts, listen actively, avoid personal blame, explore win-win options, agree on next steps, and demonstrate escalation awareness
Role-Play B (Constructive Feedback): Use Situation-Behaviour-Impact (SBI), invite perspective, maintain respectful tone, and agree on actionable revisions
Documented scenario context, student communication goals, and observable behaviours
Facilitator rubric evaluations, peer observations, and self-reflection logs
evidence: Role-Play A Evaluation Form & Reflection Log
Role-Play B Evaluation Form & Reflection Log
Facilitator behavioural critique notes
Action plan for continuous communication refinement

deliverables.name: Component 04: Group Problem-Solving Exercise
deliverables.description: Demonstrates evidence-based teamwork, structured critical thinking, constraint management, and collective decision-making in a simulated workplace project with incomplete data and unexpected changes.
required_elements: Clear definition of the core problem separating facts from assumptions
Stakeholder mapping and identification of resource/time constraints
Generation and structured comparison of at least three feasible solution alternatives
Defensible consensus or owner-driven group recommendation
Action list with task owners, risk mitigation steps, and deadlines
evidence: Problem statement and evidence analysis document
Team discussion and options comparison matrix
Final group recommendation brief with action items
Individual contribution notes and facilitator collaboration evaluation

deliverables.name: Component 05: Individual 30-Day Professional Development Plan
deliverables.description: A structured, realistic continuous improvement plan targeting high-priority workplace behaviours across three 10-day phases based on facilitator feedback, peer critiques, and self-reflection.
required_elements: Target skills, current observable baselines, and justification of professional importance
Days 01–10 (Awareness & Practice): Skill selection, observation logs, and low-stakes micro-practices
Days 11–20 (Application & Feedback): Real-world application, specific feedback gathering, and tactical adjustments
Days 21–30 (Consolidation & Review): Repetition, evidence-based self-evaluation, and setting future growth goals
Measurable progress indicators, feedback sources, and anticipated barriers
evidence: Completed 30-Day Professional Development Plan document
Baseline vs. target behavioural competency mapping
Weekly progress tracking checklist
Final portfolio assembly and reflection summary

assessment_model.title: Workplace Observable-Behaviour Assessment Rubric
criteria: Evidence-based self-reflection, work habits, and ethical judgment
Active listening: clarifying questions, accurate paraphrasing, and non-defensiveness
Perspective-taking, empathy, and professional emotional self-management
Constructive feedback delivery (SBI framework) and receptive responses to criticism
Team charter quality: clarity of roles, working agreements, and accountability
Collaborative contribution, respectful turn-taking, and inclusive participation
Realistic task prioritization, workload estimation, and adaptability to changed requirements
Critical problem-solving: separating facts from assumptions and comparing trade-offs
Routine conflict de-escalation, focus on problem vs. person, and escalation awareness
Actionable, measurable quality of the individual 30-day professional development plan
unacceptable_criteria: Personality type stereotypes (e.g. Myers-Briggs, DISC labels, extrovert vs. introvert bias)
Penalizing introverted, soft-spoken, or neurodivergent communication styles
Loudness, conversational dominance, or aggressive assertiveness mistaken for leadership
Unquestioning compliance, excessive agreement with authority, or willingness to overwork unsafely
Gendered behavioural expectations, accent conformity, or physical appearance scoring
Automated AI psychometric or emotion-recognition scoring
Conflating serious misconduct (harassment, discrimination) with negotiable routine disputes

faq.question: What is Workplace Soft Skills & Professional Effectiveness?
faq.answer: It is a practical course covering teamwork, active listening, professional responsibility, adaptability, feedback, workplace problem-solving and constructive conflict management.

faq.question: Is the course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for learners beginning professional or collaborative work, with no formal prerequisites.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Four weeks with 32 guided learning hours.

faq.question: What is the course fee?
faq.answer: ₹4,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.

faq.question: Will I learn teamwork?
faq.answer: Yes. You will practise shared responsibilities, team agreements, collaboration and group problem-solving.

faq.question: What is a Team Charter?
faq.answer: A Team Charter is a document that clarifies shared objectives, roles, responsibilities, communication practices and working expectations.

faq.question: Will I learn active listening?
faq.answer: Yes. You will practise understanding, clarifying and responding appropriately to other people's messages.

faq.question: Is emotional intelligence included?
faq.answer: Yes. The course covers applied self-awareness, empathy, perspective-taking and professional responses. It does not provide psychological diagnosis.

faq.question: Will I learn how to give feedback?
faq.answer: Yes. You will practise specific, constructive feedback and responses to criticism.

faq.question: Will I learn conflict management?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes routine workplace disagreement and conflict scenarios, with appropriate escalation awareness.

faq.question: Will I learn professional responsibility?
faq.answer: Yes. The curriculum covers accountability, work habits, ethical judgment and professional boundaries.

faq.question: Will I learn time management?
faq.answer: Yes. You will prepare a realistic prioritization plan and practise responding to competing tasks and deadlines.

faq.question: Will I learn problem-solving?
faq.answer: Yes. You will participate in an assessed collaborative exercise involving constraints, options and a justified decision.

faq.question: What practical activities are included?
faq.answer: Role-plays, small-group exercises, workplace case studies, facilitator evaluations and individual reflection.

faq.question: Will the course involve group work?
faq.answer: Yes. Guided group collaboration is a core method, with appropriate accommodations for different learning needs.

faq.question: Will I complete role-plays?
faq.answer: Yes. The portfolio includes two assessed role-plays covering workplace conflict and constructive feedback.

faq.question: Will my personality be tested?
faq.answer: No. Assessment focuses on observable professional behaviours, not fixed personality labels or psychological profiling.

faq.question: Is this suitable for introverts?
faq.answer: Yes. Professional effectiveness is not defined by extroversion. The course evaluates relevant contributions and communication behaviours.

faq.question: Do I need fluent English?
faq.answer: No advanced English fluency is universally required. Learners should confirm that the chosen batch's instruction language is suitable for them.

faq.question: Will I learn remote teamwork?
faq.answer: Yes. The course introduces basic remote collaboration, clear updates, team participation and shared task responsibilities.

faq.question: Will I learn Microsoft Teams or Google Meet?
faq.answer: These may be used for collaborative exercises, but advanced software administration is not part of the course.

faq.question: Can AI help with workplace soft skills?
faq.answer: AI can support fictional scenario practice and reflection, but it must not replace human judgment or assess personality without evidence.

faq.question: Will the course guarantee a job?
faq.answer: No. It develops useful workplace behaviours but cannot guarantee hiring, promotion or salary outcomes.

faq.question: What portfolio will I create?
faq.answer: A Team Charter, prioritization plan, two role-play evaluations, group problem-solving exercise and 30-day development plan.

faq.question: Is this course useful after technical training?
faq.answer: Yes. It complements technical skills by helping learners practise teamwork, responsibility, feedback and collaboration.

faq.question: Is this a leadership certification?
faq.answer: No. It is an applied workplace effectiveness course, not a comprehensive leadership qualification.

faq.question: Is this a psychotherapy or personality assessment program?
faq.answer: No. It is a practical professional skills program and does not provide clinical assessment or treatment.  ---
